transcript.text: Comparing chart.py with table.csv and summary.txt turns up two real defects. 1. **Country names swapped.** In the code, Senegal has GDP 820 and enrolment 115.0, and Benin has 1470 and 102.7. The table and summary have it the other way round: Benin is 820/115.0 and Senegal is 1470/102.7. The fix is to swap the two names in the Country list. I'm leaving the other columns (literacy, region) in their row positions, because only the names are misplaced. 2. **Axis labels swapped.** GDP_Per_Capita (the x axis) is labelled "Average Enrolment Rate (%)", and Average_Enrolment (the y axis) is labelled "GDP Per Capita (USD)". The summary says horizontal is GDP and vertical is enrolment, so the labels should be swapped back. Everything else matches and stays untouched, including the title, colours, size and layout. Guinea is in the table but not named in the summary. Since the table is the data source, I'm keeping it. I'll edit the file by string replacement, run it, and then read back the axis titles and the hover data from the figure to confirm. src = open('chart.py').read() src = src.replace("'Country': ['Senegal', 'Mauritania', 'Niger', 'Burkina Faso', 'Mali', 'Chad', 'Benin',", "'Country': ['Benin', 'Mauritania', 'Niger', 'Burkina Faso', 'Mali', 'Chad', 'Senegal',") src = src.replace("'GDP_Per_Capita': 'Average Enrolment Rate (%)',\n 'Average_Enrolment': 'GDP Per Capita (USD)',", "'GDP_Per_Capita': 'GDP Per Capita (USD)',\n 'Average_Enrolment': 'Average Enrolment Rate (%)',") with open('chart.py','w') as f: f.write(src) ns={} exec(src, ns) fig=ns['fig'] print(fig.layout.xaxis.title.text, '|', fig.layout.yaxis.title.text) for t in fig.data: print(t.name, list(t.x), list(t.y)) continue
